subject: CartLane workload lane mapping & token breadth — post-call
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@cartlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: CartLane workload lane mapping & token breadth — post-call

Samira — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can finalize a sizing recommendation for the PoC. TL;DR: we need the peak-window QPS, token-per-request distribution, and any streaming session duration stats so we can map lanes and compute concurrency targets.

What we heard on the call (summary):
- Target latency SLO: 200ms p95 for single-turn text-gen; 350ms p95 for streaming first-token to first-frame.
- Typical request types: short prompts (50–120 tokens) for recommendations; long-context batch edits (1k–3k tokens) for document transforms; streaming is used for live suggestions in the editor.
- Expected daily active users: 85k (projected), with peak traffic concentrated in two commercial windows: 09:30–11:00 and 17:30–18:30 PT. Peak-to-baseline multiplier they mentioned ~6–8x.

Asks (what we need from you to size lanes and tokens/sec):
1) CSV sample of 7 days of traffic showing timestamped requests with tokens_in, tokens_out, response_time_ms, and a flag for streaming_session (true/false). A 1–2 day sample is fine if 7 days is sensitive.
2) If you have a derived distribution (percentiles) for tokens per request (p50, p90, p99), include that.
3) Clarify concurrency behavior for streaming sessions: max concurrent frames/sec and average session duration.
4) Any enforced client-side rate limits (per-API-key QPS) or burst tokens that we should respect.

What we'll deliver after we get this:
- Lane mapping (short/medium/long/stream) with recommended instance types and reserved slot counts.
- Estimated QPS -> token/sec and required GPU slots for steady-state and 95th/99th peak planning.
- A simple testing harness (script + example payloads) you can run in your environment to validate latency SLOs.

Next steps: please drop the telemetry CSV to the Drive link below or reply with the file. Once we have it, Marissa and Karthik will run a quick runbook and return a draft capacity plan within 48 business hours. If helpful, we can schedule a short follow-up (30m) to walk through the sample.

Drive link for uploads: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CartLane/PoC-telemetry

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Patel <samira@cartlane.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cartlane.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:41:12 -0700
Subject: Re: CartLane workload lane mapping & token breadth — post-call

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a redacted 3-day sample (first pass) and a short notes sheet. A few clarifications inline: 

- The 6–8x multiplier is correct for user-facing windows; internal admin traffic is negligible. Peak windows are slightly different for EMEA but out of scope for this pilot.
- Tokens per request distribution (approx): p50 ~ 85 tokens, p90 ~ 420 tokens, p99 ~ 2,900 tokens. Long-context edits are ~5% of requests but contribute ~30% of token volume.
- Streaming: average session duration is ~12s, average frames/sec ~6, max observed concurrent streams in a single host region ~1,200 during peak crest (that was one day, rare).
- Client-side throttles: mobile client enforces 5 QPS per token (client-level) — not a hard server-side guard.

I uploaded cartlane_telemetry_sample.csv to the Drive link and attached a small SLA draft. Let us know if you need fuller retention data.

Best,
Samira
Sr. Engineering Manager, CartLane

Attachments: cartlane_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 2.1MB), SLA_Draft_v1.docx (DOCX, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@cartlane.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:01:37 -0700
Subject: Re: CartLane workload lane mapping & token breadth — post-call

Looping in sizing notes from a quick pass on the sample (high level):

- Observations from CSV (3-day sample):
  * Avg tokens/request (observed): ~142
  * Token-weighted QPS baseline (sample median window): ~45 tokens/sec; peak crest windows observed up to ~6.8k tokens/sec across region.
  * Long-tail events: the single-day crest had spikes that increase required capacity by ~1.9x if we want to cover 99th percentile without any fallback.

- Initial lane proposal (working draft):
  1) Short lane: <150 tokens — autoscale targets for low-latency single-turn (p95 <= 200ms).
  2) Medium lane: 150–800 tokens — batch-optimized, slightly higher tail latency acceptable (p95 <= 300ms).
  3) Long lane: >800 tokens — throughput-optimized, cost-aware (we expect 5% of requests).
  4) Streaming lane: stateful streaming pool sized for sustained concurrent streams, with burst headroom for crest.

- Questions for sizing accuracy:
  1) Can Samira confirm whether the 1,200 concurrent stream number is per-region or global? (Drive notes say single host region but want to confirm.)
  2) Any SLA exceptions for long edits during business hours (i.e., allow higher latency temporarily)?

Next steps (internal): Karthik will run token/sec -> slot conversion for the two GPU families we recommend and produce a table: steady-state slots, 95th-slot, 99th-slot and recommended reserved commit. I will produce the lane mapping doc and a short runbook to validate. Target to deliver both by EOD Wed 23 Sep.

-Marissa
Staff Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@cartlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@cartlane.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CartLane workload lane mapping & token breadth — post-call

Samira — really helpful, thank you for the files and the percentile breakdown. Quick answers:
- We see the 1,200 concurrent streams as "single-region" in our notes too; we'll size for single-region crest and add cross-region failover options later.
- No need to change the SLAs on your side for the PoC; we'll model both strict and relaxed long-edit latency bands.

Action items and schedule:
1) Karthik to run slot conversions and return a capacity table (ETA: today EOD PT).
2) Marissa to draft lane mapping + runbook and drop into the shared Drive (ETA: tomorrow EOD PT).
3) Jordan to schedule a 30m walkthrough for Thu 24 Sep 8:30–9:00 PT — Samira, does that window work?
4) Procurement: we'll include the SLA_Draft_v1 in the preliminary commercial packet; procurement, can you confirm required PO terms for a 90-day PoC?

I'll follow up with the calendar invite once Karthik confirms the slot table.

Thanks — looking forward to the PoC kickoff.

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
